title: SUIT: Secure Undervolting with Instruction Traps
problem: Modern CPUs use conservative voltage safety margins to prevent errors from aggressive undervolting, but this wastes significant energy. Too-low voltages cause security-critical errors that threaten system correctness and security.
motivation: Eliminating conservative voltage margins while preventing faults from undervolting would enable substantial energy savings in modern processors.
method: Modern CPUs run at conservative voltage levels to prevent rare errors, wasting energy—SUIT lets them run at lower voltages by catching and fixing errors when they actually occur. When voltage drops too low, special interrupt handlers (CPU interrupts that pause execution to inspect what went wrong) detect the problem and fix it by re-running the failed instruction, boosting voltage, or enabling error-correction hardware. This lets the CPU safely operate at its minimum viable voltage, saving substantial energy without risking crashes or data corruption.
key_novelty: Replace fixed voltage safety margins with dynamic error detection: instead of preventing errors upfront through conservative settings, catch and fix voltage errors as they happen.
contributions: Instruction trap-based mechanism for detecting undervolting-induced errors
Secure voltage scaling framework removing conservative safety margins
Hardware-software co-design enabling aggressive dynamic voltage scaling
Energy efficiency improvements while maintaining security and reliability

metrics.energy_or_tops_w: energy savings from reduced voltage margins
metrics.other: fault detection coverage and recovery success rate

baselines: Stock voltage scaling with safety margins
limitations: Performance overhead of fault detection and recovery, scalability to multi-core systems, and applicability to different instruction types not discussed.
primary_theme: secure aggressive voltage scaling via fault detection
